newsitem.title: ITALY: Ciampi says Italy will seek ERM re-entry mid-Nov.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi says Italy will seek ERM re-entry mid-Nov.

text.p: Italy aims to seek re-entry to Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) after the 1997 budget has cleared the lower house of parliament, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said in an interview published on Friday.
"Our aim is not to wait for complete approval of the budget," Ciampi told financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore.
"The moment could be the vote in the Chamber...At that point, I believe we could put forward a request to our European partners," he said.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's 1997 austerity budget, which aims to cut 62.5 trillion lire off next year's deficit, is scheduled to go before the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) on October 30 and to complete its passage there by November 14.
Prodi has repeatedly said he intends to get the lira back into the ERM, which it crashed out of amid currency turmoil in September 1992, before the end of the year.
Ciampi said the biggest problem was the central parity of the lira against other currencies.
"We're now at an exchange rate that, on average in the last few months, is 1,020 to 1,030 (against the mark)," Ciampi said.
Analysts said the idea of a central lira rate of around 1,000 per mark is taking root in the market.

The lira was trading near 1,004 on Friday morning. Some of Italy's European partners are worried about the lira's volatility and France, in particular, is unhappy with the compeititive edge Italy has gained via a weaker currency since the lira was ejected from the ERM.
Analysts said Paris would prefer a firmer rather than a weaker lira to help its own exporters.
Italy needs to get the lira back into the ERM by year-end in order to have a chance of qualifying for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
"I entered the Prodi government for one reason, for one specific duty -- to take Italy into Europe (monetary union)," Ciampi told the newspaper.
